findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(i) Observed a cutting board being stored behind the handles of the triple sink. CORRECTED: PIC moved the cutting board to a place where it can air-dry and not be contaminated from spills. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
(ii) Observed one of the nozzles from the drink dispenser had an accumulation of soils. CORRECTED: Staff removed the nozzles for washing, rinsing, and sanitizing. Nozzles should be cleaned at a frequency to keep the food-contact surfaces clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed that the door for the right walk-in cooler is damaged, requiring significant effort to open and keep shut. Duct tape has been added to the handle to provide for a better grip. The PIC was notified. Ensure that equipment components for doors and hinges are kept intact, tight, and properly adjusted.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed equipment that needs more frequent cleaning:
(i) the sliding doors behind the storage shelves.
(ii) the doors on both sides of the 6-compartment cooler (currently used for equipment storage).
(iii) the bottom part of the oven.
(iv) the sides of the front area grill.
(v) the back walls underneath the hood behind the grill and fryers.
Ensure that these areas are cleaned with regular frequency to keep them clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed several pieces of equipment that are in disrepair, are no longer working and should be removed from service, or are not in service and should be removed if they will not be cleaned frequently:
(i) The reach-in freezer lid is broken; the lid no longer stays upright when opened, and it can potentially injure employees when it slams shut; the visible damage to the lid is no longer smooth and easily cleanable.
(ii) The middle walk-in cooler has a steady drip that needs to be fixed; staff placed a catch basin to catch the drip during the inspection.
(iii) The sanitizer dispenser hose for the triple sink is not dispensing enough sanitizer in a timely manner, requiring several minutes of running to reach an effective quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution. Staff cannot fill their sanitizing buckets from the dispenser hose; instead staff must scoop sanitizing solution from a full triple sink.
(iv) The automatic paper towel dispenser in the serving area is damaged and not dispensing paper towels; staff are using a separate paper towel roll to complete handwashing.
(v) The prep sink in the back kitchen is not working; it is no longer being used to prepare food.
(vi) The 2-door cooler in the back kitchen is not working due to a drip issue; it is no longer being used for cold-holding or for dry goods storage.
(vii) The 1-door hot box in the back kitchen is broken beyond repair; it is still waiting to be removed from the facility.
(viii) The pizza oven is no longer being used, as pizza is not made by the establishment.
Ensure physical equipment is either maintained in good repair or removed from service.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee used their bare hands to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated during the inspection and proceeded to use the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed the scoops for the sugar and powered sugar were stored with the handles touching the food. The PIC was educated and the scoops were removed from the containers during the inspection. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to prevent bare hand contact with the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the front hand washing sink did not have paper towels available when the inspectors arrived at the facility. The PIC brought paper towels to the hand washing sink during the inspection. Ensure that there is always paper towels available at every hand washing sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed there is a significant accumulation of mold inside both of the walk-in coolers. The mold accumulation is on the walls, ceilings, and shelving. The coolers must be cleaned to sight and touch to avoid cross contamination with food. The inspector will follow-up on 1/14/2025 to check that both walk-in coolers have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order:

(1) Raw hamburger patties above various sauces in the front prep cooler. 

(2) Raw chicken over containers of milk in the right walk-in cooler. 

The storage order violations were corrected during the inspection. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the shelves above the triple sink have an accumulation of debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the shelving is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The food debris and grease on the floor underneath the front grill and steam table. 

(2) The dust on the wall vent behind the front steam table. 

(3) The food debris and grease on the floor underneath the kitchen fryers - THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Observed there is a leak at the kitchen hand washing sink from the faucet spout. Ensure that the leak is repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a mop stored with the wet head directly on the ground. The PIC hung the mop inverted during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored with the mop head in a position that facilitates air drying.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed containers of mashed potatoes, fried chicken, and baked chicken in the right walk-in cooler prepared last week that were not date marked. The PIC voluntarily discarded the foods during the inspection. The PIC was educated that ready-to-eat, temperature control for safety foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum (with the day the food was prepared being day 1). Ensure that all foods are correctly date marked by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed containers of sugar, powdered sugar, and flour were not labeled. The inspector educated that all containers holding white powders (and other easily mistakable foods) must be labeled with the common name of the food. The PIC labeled the containers during the inspection. Ensure that all easily mistakable foods not in their original packages are always labeled.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of food debris and grease underneath the fryers in the kitchen. The PIC was reminded that physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of food, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the floor under the fryers is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that several employees have expired food handler certificates. All employees that handle food and do not have a CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must take the class. Ensure that all required employees obtain food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a CFPM at the facility when the inspector arrived. During the inspection a CFPM (Lindsay Prior) arrived. Currently she is the only CFPM at the facility. The inspector suggests getting more employees certified since she works in both the Stratton and Howlett buildings. Ensure there is always a CFPM at the facility during all hours of operation.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed several foods (including, but not limited to, chicken, tater tots, and garlic bread) stored in the triple freezer uncovered. The foods were covered during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always protected from cross contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed cutting boards drying behind the facet of the triple sink. Storing the cutting boards in this position presents the risk of contamination from food debris or dirty water splashes. The cutting boards were re-sanitized and placed in a new position to air-dry during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces remain clean to sight and touch. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed to-go foods in the front display coolers (including, but not limited to, fruit cups, pudding, yogurt, and pasta salad) lacking proper date marking. Food kept at the establishment for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum (the day food is prepared is day 1). The required foods were date marked during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always properly date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed display cooler #1 and display cooler #2 (two coolers closest to the cook line) are not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The TCS foods inside had internal temperatures between 43F to 45F and were moved into different functioning coolers. The PIC stated they will be getting the coolers serviced. The inspector will return on 11/25/2024 to check that the coolers have been repaired. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet wiping cloths stored on the side of sink basins drying. The inspector educated that wet wiping cloths must be stored in chemical sanitizer between uses. The wiping cloths were discarded during the inspection. Ensure that in-use wiping cloths are stored in chemical saniztier between uses and laundered daily. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the shelves above the triple sink holding clean pots and other cooking equipment are soiled with debris. Non-food contact surfaces (even those hard to reach) must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that the shelf is cleaned by the next routine inspection. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed that no one at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training. The inspector suggests the PIC and other employees complete the training. Ensure that CFPM’s complete their allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed utensils (spoons and forks) in the customer condiment area being stored with the handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. Utensils must be stored so only handles are touched by customers. The PIC moved the utensils into a position where the food contact surfaces are facing in the same direction during the inspection. Ensure that utensils are stored in a position where customers are only touching handles. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop was stored sitting on a paper surface. Non-food contact surfaces must be smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. The PIC stated they are going to store the ice scoop in a container instead of directly on the paper surface. Ensure that the ice scoop is stored on a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the shelves above the triple sink holding clean pots and other equipment are soiled with debris. Nonfood contact surfaces of equipment (even those hard to reach) must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that the shelf is cleaned by the next routine inspection. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed that no one at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that CFPM’s complete their allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There is no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) in charge of the facility during the inspection and serving time today. The facility shall be under the control of a CFPM at all times food is being prepared or served. Facility manager stated that they are looking to get another certified manager. Provide enough CFPMs to have coverage of both sites at all times. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the blades of both can openers are soiled with food debris. The can opener blades were washed, rinsed and sanitized at the time of inspection. Maintain food contacts surfaces cleaned and sanitized. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Food on the hot serving line was evaluated with a probe thermometer to be  BBQ 119F and Meatloaf 122F. Mashed potatoes were stirred and temped with an IR thermometer to be 98F. As the food was below 135 for an undetermined amount of time staff was directed to discard the food and not attempt to cool the food or save it for another service day. According to staff the food items were placed on the steam table between 10:30 11am. The food was served for approximately two and a half hours. Food temperature logs were not recorded today. If time as a control for safety is used then food shall be discarded after use. If temperature control for safety is used then the food shall be 135F or above. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a purse, cell phone, cash money, and a pack of facial cleaning cloths on the prep table next to a box of gloves. The desk with other employee belongings is less than 5 feet from this area. Store employee belongings properly separated from food service items. 

6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed there to be two bags of food in the chest freezer in the back room of the kitchen which were left open. Ensure that containers of food in the chest freezers remain closed while being stored to prevent contamination of the foods inside. Operator closed the bags during the inspection. Corrected on site. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Above the wooden countertop at the rear of the kitchen is a shelf with a container of sugar which was observed to have a scoop sitting inside it with the handle stored inside the sugar itself. Ensure that all utensils are stored with handles pointing upward to prevent contact with the foods stored within the containers. Operator immediately removed the scoop from the container. Corrected on site. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION(S)

During the previous inspection, the walk-in freezer had failed and foods were removed from the freezer and placed in chest freezers. The freezer remains is disrepair and is unable to be used. Further, the walk-in cooler has now failed as well resulting in further decreased cold-storage capacity at this facility. Both the walk-in freezer and walk-in cooler must be repaired by the next routine inspection. Ensure that all equipment remains in good repair. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a plastic bottle of degreaser stored directly above the cleaned and sanitized dishes at the far right side of the triple sink. Poisonous chemicals must be stored in a manner that prevents contamination. Such chemicals must never be stored above food or food-contact surfaces. Ensure that chemicals are stored properly at all times. The bottle of degreaser was immediately moved and stored underneath the counter. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Upon arrival to the facility, operators advised the inspector that the walk-in freezer had failed completely and walk-in cooler is functioning but unable to maintain a temperature sufficiently low to ensure food temepratures are maintained at 41 degrees F or below at all times without frequent recharging of the condenser. Chest freezers have been brought in to supplement the failed equipment until repairs can be made. Foods are maintained within proper temperatures and all frozen foods have remained frozen. Foods were discarded by staff prior to the inspection if out of temperature as a result of the equipment malfunction. The walk-in freezer and cooler are intended to be used and as such must remain in good repair at all times. Ensure that all equipment in-use in the facility is in good repair by the next routine inspection in 2023. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed mold residue on ice machine. Ensure ice machine is cleaned as needed to prevent accumulation. Clean Ice machine. 
Observed single-service serving cups to be setting in containers with accumulated food debris. Ensure single-service items are placed in clean area. Clean containers.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed sausage to be 122F on Steam table. PIC stated sausage has been present on table for ~1 hour. Rapidly reheat sausage to 165F. Corrected.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) ***** is ***** °F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to above 165°F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).
